parts.content:
Questions 1–10
Complete the notes below.
Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

Ferry to Shetland Islands
• Name of ferry company: 1 ............... Ferries
• Ferries depart seven times per 2 ............... in summer
• Cost for four people with car: a little less than 3 £ ...............
• Cancellation policy: receive a 4 ............... (if cancelled a month in advance)

Advice
• Cabins:
  book one with a 5 ...............
  luxury cabins have a TV
• Bring snacks and 6 ............... for the children
• A 7 ............... is required for the dog kennels
• Try to see 8 ............... in the morning
• If time, visit 9 ............... Castle
• The 10 ............... restaurant in a nearby village is recommended

parts.title: Section 2
parts.content:
Questions 11 and 12
Choose TWO letters, A–E.
Which TWO facilities are available at the newly refurbished youth hostel?
A a climbing wall
B a heated swimming pool
C a bicycle repair workshop
D a laundry room
E a communal kitchen

Questions 13 and 14
Choose TWO letters, A–E.
Which TWO activities are recommended for rainy days?
A visiting the transport museum
B exploring the underground caverns
C touring the woollen mill
D attending a pottery workshop
E watching a film at the historic cinema

Questions 15 and 16
Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

15 Why is booking recommended for the guided walk along the gorge?
A It is only offered on certain days of the week.
B Group sizes are strictly limited.
C The guide is an internationally known expert.

16 What does the speaker say about public transport to the coastal nature reserve?
A Buses run every fifteen minutes.
B Tickets must be bought in advance online.
C The service does not operate on Sundays.

Questions 17–20
What should visitors bear in mind about each of the following attractions?
Choose FOUR answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–F, next to Questions 17–20.

A Sturdy footwear is essential.
B Entry is free for children under twelve.
C Photography is prohibited inside the building.
D It is advisable to bring warm clothing.
E Mobile phone reception is unavailable.
F Food cannot be purchased on site.

Attractions
17 High Crag Lighthouse
18 Blackwood Forest Trail
19 Old Watermill
20 Beacon Hill Lookout

parts.title: Section 3
parts.content:
Questions 21 and 22
Choose TWO letters, A–E.
Which TWO properties of semi-synthetic fabrics make them popular in the fashion industry?
A their resistance to tearing
B their biodegradable nature
C their ability to absorb bright dyes
D their low manufacturing cost
E their breathability in hot climates

Questions 23 and 24
Choose TWO letters, A–E.
Which TWO environmental problems associated with viscose production do the students emphasize?
A deforestation caused by harvesting raw timber
B high energy use during spinning
C microplastic shedding in domestic washing
D toxic chemical release into rivers
E excessive water consumption in processing

Questions 25–30
What comment do the speakers make about each of the following semi-synthetic fibres?
Choose SIX answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–H, next to Questions 25–30.

Comments
A It requires chemicals that are hard to neutralise.
B It is made using a closed-loop solvent system.
C It has superior fire resistance.
D It is derived from waste agricultural products.
E It has been banned in several European countries.
F Its production is currently too expensive for mass markets.
G It produces exceptionally smooth yarn.
H It requires less land than conventional cotton.

Fibres
25 Modal
26 Lyocell (Tencel)
27 Cupro
28 Bamboo viscose
29 Orange fibre
30 Seaweed-based fabric

parts.title: Section 4
parts.content:
Questions 31–40
Complete the notes below.
Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

Invasive marine species
Introduction of alien species
• Global shipping has accelerated the introduction of non-native organisms
• Ballast water discharged into ports is a key pathway for spreading 31 ...............
• Alien species disrupt the balance of the local 32 ...............

Case studies
• Mediterranean Sea:
  Caulerpa taxifolia (alga) escaped from an aquarium and covered vast underwater areas
  Spread was aided by recreational boats during the summer 33 ............... season
• Caribbean lionfish:
  Likely released by private owners of exotic 34 ...............
  Voracious predators consuming juvenile reef fish in huge numbers
• Comb jellies in the Black Sea:
  Fed heavily on zooplankton, starving native anchovies
  Damaged the commercial fishing industry and reduced local 35 ............... production

Control and prevention strategies
• Ballast water treatment:
  Using filtration, heat, or ultraviolet 36 ............... before discharge
• Biological control:
  Careful introduction of a specific natural predator or 37 ............... to target pests
• Monitoring and community science:
  Tracking changes in marine species 38 ...............
  Encouraging divers to upload sighting data to an online 39 ...............
  Every record should include coordinates and a clear 40 ............... for verification
